question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: To achieve a complete cure of the genetic mutation
options.B: To stop the natural progression of the disease entirely
options.C: To reverse the physical breakdown of body tissues
options.D: To maximize remaining function and quality of life

explanation: Because these genetic disorders are progressive and incurable, rehabilitation focuses on maintaining independence and quality of life rather than reversing the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h1)

question: Why is a complete cure not the main goal of rehabilitation in degenerative genetic conditions?

options.A: Rehabilitation therapies only work on non-genetic illnesses
options.B: Hospitals lack the proper equipment to reverse genetic changes
options.C: Patients refuse to participate in long-term treatment programs
options.D: The conditions involve continuous, progressive breakdown of tissues

explanation: Since these conditions involve ongoing tissue breakdown, therapy is all about managing symptoms and helping patients adapt, rather than fixing the root genetic cause. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h1)

question: What physical change directly leads to a loss of independence in degenerative muscle disorders?
explanation: As muscle fibers waste away and weaken, patients gradually lose the physical strength needed to move and care for themselves. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h2)

question: Why does functional decline in degenerative disorders often fluctuate day-to-day?

options.A: Immune systems fight off the genetic code
options.C: Genetic mutations change their sequence daily
options.D: Patients experience varying levels of fatigue and stiffness

explanation: Factors like exhaustion, muscle stiffness, and small changes in health can cause daily ups and downs in what a patient is able to do. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h2)

question: Who should be involved when setting rehabilitation goals for a patient with a degenerative disorder?

options.A: Only the physical therapist and the patient
options.B: The healthcare team, the patient, and their family
options.C: Only the doctor and the hospital administrator
options.D: The insurance provider and the nursing supervisor

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Effective goal setting requires input from everyone involved in the patient's care to ensure targets are realistic and meaningful. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h3)

question: Why is anticipating future needs an important part of nursing care in degenerative conditions?

options.A: It stops the genetic disorder from spreading to family members
options.B: It allows the team to prepare equipment and home changes before skills are lost
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will regain full mobility
options.D: It removes the need for ongoing nursing assessments

explanation: Thinking ahead means assistive devices and home changes can be arranged proactively, reducing stress and avoiding last-minute crises. Brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of gentle stretching exercises in degenerative disorders?
explanation: Gentle stretching keeps joints flexible and helps stop the painful tightening of muscles and tendons known as contractures. You are mastering this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: A patient with a degenerative condition frequently becomes exhausted halfway through a morning walk. What physical therapy strategy should be introduced?

options.B: Complete bed rest to eliminate all physical exertion
options.C: Immediate removal of all walking aids
options.D: High-intensity weight lifting to build sudden bulk

explanation: Teaching the patient to pace themselves and conserve energy helps them stay active without burning out all their strength at once. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy for individuals with degenerative disorders?

options.C: Assisting with daily activities like dressing and eating

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients maintain independence in personal care and household tasks through smart adaptations. Great job! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: How do modified utensils with built-in grips help a patient with failing fine motor control?

options.A: They compensate for weak grip strength and hand tremors
options.B: They completely cure the underlying nerve degeneration
options.C: They prevent the patient from feeling hungry
options.D: They make the food taste better and digest faster

explanation: Specialized grips provide better purchase for weak hands, allowing the patient to continue feeding themselves without assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What term describes the swallowing difficulties caused by muscle weakness in degenerative disorders?
explanation: Dysphagia is the medical term for difficulty swallowing—something we must watch out for closely to prevent food or liquid from entering the airway. You're doing awesome! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: Why might a speech-language pathologist recommend thickened liquids for a patient with a degenerative condition?

options.A: To increase the patient's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To cure the underlying inflammation in the throat muscles
options.C: To make the drink taste more appealing to the patient
options.D: To prevent the liquid from moving too fast and causing aspiration

explanation: Thickened liquids move slower down the throat, giving weakened swallowing muscles more time to close the airway and prevent choking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: Which emotional challenge is commonly experienced by family caregivers of patients with degenerative disorders?

options.D: Sudden loss of all personal memories

explanation: Providing round-the-clock care for a progressively worsening condition can heavily drain family members, making caregiver support a vital part of nursing. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h7)

question: Why is addressing emotional and mental health considered essential in rehabilitative care?

options.A: Mental health support can reverse genetic mutations in the brain
options.B: Psychological counseling replaces the need for physical exercises
options.C: Emotional distress can worsen physical symptoms and reduce coping
options.D: Families do not require any support until the final stages of illness

explanation: Mental and emotional health directly impacts a patient's willingness and ability to participate in rehabilitation and enjoy daily life. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in advanced degenerative disorders?

options.A: Stopping all forms of nursing care

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and distressing symptoms to ensure the patient remains comfortable and maintains their dignity. Beautiful nursing philosophy! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)

question: Why is palliative care ideally introduced before the very final days of a degenerative illness?

options.A: To allow a smooth transition and build relationships with the care team
options.B: To guarantee that the patient will regain full physical mobility
options.C: To speed up the natural progression of the genetic disorder
options.D: To eliminate the need for any medications or nursing oversight

explanation: Early introduction helps patients and families process difficult decisions and builds trust with the palliative team before a crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)
